\\"ip\_address\\", \\"name\\"]\\n        },\\n        \\"user\\": {\\n          \\"type\\": \\"object\\",\\n          \\"properties\\": {\\n            \\"id\\": { \\"type\\": \\"string\\", \\"format\\": \\"uuid\\" },\\n            \\"aud\\": { \\"type\\": \\"string\\" },\\n            \\"role\\": { \\"type\\": \\"string\\" },\\n            \\"email\\": { \\"type\\": \\"string\\", \\"format\\": \\"email\\" },\\n            \\"phone\\": { \\"type\\": \\"string\\" },\\n            \\"app\_metadata\\": {\\n              \\"type\\": \\"object\\",\\n              \\"properties\\": {\\n                \\"provider\\": { \\"type\\": \\"string\\" },\\n                \\"providers\\": {\\n                  \\"type\\": \\"array\\",\\n                  \\"items\\": { \\"type\\": \\"string\\" }\\n                }\\n              },\\n              \\"required\\": \[\\"provider\\", \\"providers\\"]\\n            },\\n            \\"user\_metadata\\": { \\"type\\": \\"object\\" },\\n            \\"identities\\": {\\n              \\"type\\": \\"array\\",\\n              \\"items\\": { \\"type\\": \\"object\\" }\\n            },\\n            \\"created\_at\\": { \\"type\\": \\"string\\", \\"format\\": \\"date-time\\" },\\n            \\"updated\_at\\": { \\"type\\": \\"string\\", \\"format\\": \\"date-time\\" },\\n            \\"is\_anonymous\\": { \\"type\\": \\"boolean\\" }\\n          },\\n          \\"required\\": \[\\n            \\"id\\",\\n            \\"aud\\",\\n            \\"role\\",\\n            \\"email\\",\\n            \\"phone\\",\\n            \\"app\_metadata\\",\\n            \\"user\_metadata\\",\\n            \\"identities\\",\\n            \\"created\_at\\",\\n            \\"updated\_at\\",\\n            \\"is\_anonymous\\"\\n          ]\\n        }\\n      },\\n      \\"required\\": \[\\"metadata\\", \\"user\\"]\\n    }\\n    ```\\n  </TabPanel>\\n</Tabs>\\n\\n\\n## Outputs\\n\\nYour hook must return a response that either allows or blocks the signup request.\\n\\n| Field   | Type     | Description                                                                                           |\\n| ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\\n| `error` | `object` | (Optional) Return this to reject the signup. Includes a code, message, and optional HTTP status code. |\\n\\nReturning an empty object with a `200` or `204` status code allows the request to proceed. Returning a JSON response with an `error` object and a `4xx` status code blocks the request and propagates the error message to the client. See the \[error handling documentation](/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks#error-handling) for more details.\\n\\n\\n### Allow the signup\\n\\n```json\\n{}\\n```\\n\\nor with a `204 No Content` response:\\n\\n```http\\nHTTP/1.1 204 No Content\\n```\\n\\n\\n### Reject the signup with an error\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\"error\\": {\\n    \\"http\_code\\": 400,\\n    \\"message\\": \\"Only company emails are allowed to sign up.\\"\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThis response will block the user creation and return the error message to the client that attempted signup.\\n\\n\\n## Examples\\n\\nEach of the following examples shows how to use the `before-user-created` hook to control signup behavior. Each use case includes both an HTTP implementation (e.g. using an Edge Function) and a SQL implementation (Postgres function).\\n\\n<Tabs scrollable size=\\"small\\" type=\\"underlined\\" defaultActiveId=\\"sql\\" queryGroup=\\"language\\">\\n  <TabPanel id=\\"sql\\" label=\\"SQL\\">\\n    <Tabs scrollable size=\\"small\\" type=\\"underlined\\" defaultActiveId=\\"sql-allow-by-domain\\">\\n      <TabPanel id=\\"sql-allow-by-domain\\" label=\\"Allow by Domain\\">\\n        Allow signups only from specific domains like supabase.com or example.test. Reject all others. This is useful for private/internal apps, enterprise gating, or invite-only beta access.\\n\\n        The `before-user-created` hook solves this by:\\n\\n        \*   Detecting that a user is about to be created\\n        \*   Providing the email address in the `user.email` field\\n\\n        Run the following snippet in your project's \[SQL Editor](/dashboard/project/\_/sql/new). This will create a `signup\_email\_domains` table with some sample data and a `hook\_restrict\_signup\_by\_email\_domain` function to be called by the `before-user-created` auth hook.\\n\\n        ```sql\\n        -- Create ENUM type for domain rule classification\\n        do $$ begin\\n          create type signup\_email\_domain\_type as enum ('allow', 'deny');\\n        exception\\n          when duplicate\_object then null;\\n        end $$;\\n\\n        -- Create the signup\_email\_domains table\\n        create table if not exists public.signup\_email\_domains (\\n          id serial primary key,\\n          domain text not null,\\n          type signup\_email\_domain\_type not null,\\n          reason text default null,\\n          created\_at timestamptz not null default now(),\\n          updated\_at timestamptz not null default now()\\n        );\\n\\n        -- Create a trigger to maintain updated\_at\\n        create or replace function update\_signup\_email\_domains\_updated\_at()\\n        returns trigger as $$\\n        begin\\n          new.updated\_at = now();\\n          return new;\\n        end;\\n        $$ language plpgsql;\\n\\n        drop trigger if exists trg\_signup\_email\_domains\_set\_updated\_at on public.signup\_email\_domains;\\n\\n        create trigger trg\_signup\_email\_domains\_set\_updated\_at\\n        before update on public.signup\_email\_domains\\n        for each row\\n        execute procedure update\_signup\_email\_domains\_updated\_at();\\n\\n        -- Seed example data\\n        insert into public.signup\_email\_domains (domain, type, reason) values\\n          ('supabase.com', 'allow', 'Internal signups'),\\n          ('gmail.com', 'deny', 'Public email provider'),\\n          ('yahoo.com', 'deny', 'Public email provider');\\n\\n        -- Create the function\\n        create or replace function public.hook\_restrict\_signup\_by\_email\_domain(event jsonb)\\n        returns jsonb\\n        language plpgsql\\n        as $$\\n        declare\\n          email text;\\n          domain text;\\n          is\_allowed int;\\n          is\_denied int;\\n        begin\\n          email := event->'user'->>'email';\\n          domain := split\_part(email, '@', 2);\\n\\n          -- Check for allow match\\n          select count(\*) into is\_allowed\\n          from public.signup\_email\_domains\\n          where type = 'allow' and lower(domain) = lower($1);\\n\\n          if is\_allowed > 0 then\\n            return '{}'::jsonb;\\n          end if;\\n\\n          -- Check for deny match\\n          select count(\*) into is\_denied\\n          from public.signup\_email\_domains\\n          where type = 'deny' and lower(domain) = lower($1);\\n\\n          if is\_denied > 0 then\\n            return jsonb\_build\_object(\\n              'error', jsonb\_build\_object(\\n                'message', 'Signups from this email domain are not allowed.',\\n                'http\_code', 403\\n              )\\n            );\\n          end if;\\n\\n          -- No match, allow by default\\n          return '{}'::jsonb;\\n        end;\\n        $$;\\n\\n        -- Permissions\\n        grant execute\\n          on function public.hook\_restrict\_signup\_by\_email\_domain\\n          to supabase\_auth\_admin;\\n\\n        revoke execute\\n          on function public.hook\_restrict\_signup\_by\_email\_domain\\n          from authenticated, anon, public;\\n        ```\\n      </TabPanel>\\n\\n      <TabPanel id=\\"sql-block-by-oauth-provider\\" label=\\"Block by OAuth Provider\\">\\n        Some applications want to \*\*allow sign-ins with a provider like Discord only for users who already exist\*\*, while blocking new account creation via that provider. This prevents unwanted signups through OAuth flows and enables tighter control over who can join the app.\\n\\n        The `before-user-created` hook solves this by:\\n\\n        \*   Detecting that a user is about to be created\\n        \*   Allowing you to inspect the `app\_metadata.provider`\\n        \*   Knowing the request came from an OAuth flow\\n\\n        Run the following snippet in your project's \[SQL Editor](/dashboard/project/\_/sql/new). This will create a `hook\_reject\_discord\_signups` function to be called by the `before-user-created` auth hook.\\n\\n        ```sql\\n        -- Create the function\\n        create or replace function public.hook\_reject\_discord\_signups(event jsonb)\\n        returns jsonb\\n        language plpgsql\\n        as $$\\n        declare\\n          provider text;\\n        begin\\n          provider := event->'user'->'app\_metadata'->>'provider';\\n\\n          if provider = 'discord' then\\n            return jsonb\_build\_object(\\n              'error', jsonb\_build\_object(\\n                'message', 'Signups with Discord are not allowed.',\\n                'http\_code', 403\\n              )\\n            );\\n          end if;\\n\\n          return '{}'::jsonb;\\n        end;\\n        $$;\\n\\n        -- Permissions\\n        grant execute\\n          on function public.hook\_reject\_discord\_signups\\n          to supabase\_auth\_admin;\\n\\n        revoke execute\\n          on function public.hook\_reject\_discord\_signups\\n          from authenticated, anon, public;\\n        ```\\n      </TabPanel>\\n\\n      <TabPanel id=\\"sql-allow-deny-by-cidr\\" label=\\"Allow/Deny by IP or CIDR\\">\\n        This example shows how you might restrict sign up from a single IP address or a range of them using \[Postgres’s built-in](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype-net-types.html) `inet` and `<<` operators for \[CIDR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classless\_Inter-Domain\_Routing) -- a method of representing IP address ranges.\\n        For instance: `123.123.123.123/32` represents only a single IP address, while `123.123.123.0/24` means all IP addresses starting with `123.123.123.`.\\n\\n        The `before-user-created` hook solves this by:\\n\\n        \*   Detecting that a user is about to be created\\n        \*   Providing the IP address in the `metadata.ip\_address` field\\n\\n        Run the following snippet in your project's \[SQL Editor](/dashboard/project/\_/sql/new). This will create a `signup\_networks` table with some sample data and a `hook\_restrict\_signup\_by\_network` function to be called by the `before-user-created` auth hook.\\n\\n        ```sql SQL\_EDITOR\\n        -- Create ENUM type for network rule classification\\n        create type signup\_network\_type as enum ('allow', 'deny');\\n\\n        -- Create the signup\_networks table for controlling sign-up access by CIDR\\n        create table if not exists public.signup\_networks (\\n          id serial primary key,\\n          cidr cidr not null,\\n          type public.signup\_network\_type not null,\\n          reason text default null,\\n          note text default null,\\n          created\_at timestamp with time zone not null default now(),\\n          constraint signup\_networks\_cidr\_key unique (cidr)\\n        );\\n\\n        -- Assign appropriate permissions\\n        grant all\\n          on table public.signup\_networks\\n          to supabase\_auth\_admin;\\n\\n        revoke all\\n          on table public.signup\_networks\\n          from authenticated, anon, public;\\n\\n        -- Insert some sample data into the table\\n        insert into public.signup\_networks (cidr, type, reason, note)\\n        values\\n          ('192.0.2.0/24', 'allow', '', 'Corporate VPN'),\\n          ('198.51.100.158/32', 'deny',\\n            'Your IP Address has been blocked for abuse.',\\n            'blocked by abuse: (Ticket: ABUSE-185)'),\\n          ('203.0.113.0/24', 'deny',\\n            'Your network has been blocked for abuse.',\\n            'blocked by abuse: (Ticket: ABUSE-212)');\\n\\n        -- Create the hook function to be called by the auth server\\n        create or replace function public.hook\_restrict\_signup\_by\_network(event jsonb)\\n        returns jsonb\\n        language plpgsql\\n        as $$\\n        declare\\n          ip inet;\\n          allow\_count int;\\n          deny\_count int;\\n        begin\\n          ip := event->'metadata'->>'ip\_address';\\n\\n          -- Step 1: Check for explicit allow\\n          select count(\*) into allow\_count\\n          from public.signup\_networks\\n          where type = 'allow' and ip::inet << cidr;\\n\\n          if allow\_count > 0 then\\n            -- If explicitly allowed, allow signup\\n            return '{}'::jsonb;\\n          end if;\\n\\n          -- Step 2: Check for explicit deny\\n          select count(\*) into deny\_count\\n          from public.signup\_networks\\n          where type = 'deny' and ip::inet << cidr;\\n\\n          if deny\_count > 0 then\\n            return jsonb\_build\_object(\\n              'error', jsonb\_build\_object(\\n                'message', 'Signups are not allowed from your network.',\\n                'http\_code', 403\\n              )\\n            );\\n          end if;\\n\\n          -- Step 3: No match: allow by default\\n          return '{}'::jsonb;\\n        end;\\n        $$;\\n\\n        -- Assign permissions\\n        grant execute\\n          on function public.hook\_restrict\_signup\_by\_network\\n          to supabase\_auth\_admin;\\n\\n        revoke execute\\n          on function public.hook\_restrict\_signup\_by\_network\\n          from authenticated, anon, public;\\n        ```\\n      </TabPanel>\\n    </Tabs>\\n  </TabPanel>\\n\\n  <TabPanel id=\\"http\\" label=\\"HTTP\\">\\n    <Tabs scrollable size=\\"small\\" type=\\"underlined\\" defaultActiveId=\\"http-allow-by-domain\\">\\n      <TabPanel id=\\"http-allow-by-domain\\" label=\\"Allow by Domain\\">\\n        Allow signups only from specific domains like supabase.com or example.test. Reject all others. This is useful for private/internal apps, enterprise gating, or invite-only beta access.\\n\\n        The `before-user-created` hook solves this by:\\n\\n        \*   Detecting that a user is about to be created\\n        \*   Providing the email address in the `user.email` field\\n\\n        Create a `.env` file with the following environment variables:\\n\\n        ```ini\\n        BEFORE\_USER\_CREATED\_HOOK\_SECRET=\\"v1,whsec\_<base64\_secret>\\"\\n        ```\\n\\n        <Admonition type=\\"note\\">\\n          You can generate the secret in the \[Auth Hooks](/dashboard/project/\_/auth/hooks) section of the Supabase dashboard.\\n        </Admonition>\\n\\n        Set the secrets in your Supabase project:\\n\\n        ```bash\\n        supabase secrets set --env-file .env\\n        ```\\n\\n        Create a new edge function:\\n\\n        ```bash\\n        supabase functions new before-user-created-hook\\n        ```\\n\\n        Add the following code to your edge function:\\n\\n        ```ts\\n        import { Webhook } from 'https://esm.sh/standardwebhooks@1.0.0'\\n\\n        const allowedDomains = \['supabase.com', 'example.test']\\n\\n        Deno.serve(async (req) => {\\n          const payload = await req.text()\\n          const secret = Deno.env.get('BEFORE\_USER\_CREATED\_HOOK\_SECRET')?.replace('v1,whsec\_', '')\\n          const headers = Object.fromEntries(req.headers)\\n          const wh = new Webhook(secret)\\n\\n          try {\\n            const { user } = wh.verify(payload, headers)\\n            const email = user.email || ''\\n            const domain = email.split('@')\[1] || ''\\n\\n            if (!allowedDomains.includes(domain)) {\\n              return new Response(\\n                JSON.stringify({\\n                  error: {\\n                    message: 'Please sign up with a company email address.',\\n                    http\_code: 400,\\n                  },\\n                }),\\n                { status: 400, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }\\n              )\\n            }\\n\\n            return new Response('{}', { status: 200, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } })\\n          } catch (error) {\\n            return new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: { message: 'Invalid request format' } }), {\\n              status: 400,\\n              headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\\n            })\\n          }\\n        })\\n        ```\\n      </TabPanel>\\n\\n      <TabPanel id=\\"http-block-by-oauth-provider\\" label=\\"Block by OAuth Provider\\">\\n        Some applications want to \*\*allow sign-ins with a provider like Discord only for users who already exist\*\*, while blocking new account creation via that provider. This prevents unwanted signups through OAuth flows and enables tighter control over who can join the app.\\n\\n        The `before-user-created` hook solves this by:\\n\\n        \*   Allowing you to inspect the `app\_metadata.provider`\\n        \*   Detecting that a user is about to be created\\n        \*   Knowing the request came from an OAuth flow\\n\\n        Create a `.env` file with the following environment variables:\\n\\n        ```ini\\n        BEFORE\_USER\_CREATED\_HOOK\_SECRET=\\"v1,whsec\_<base64\_secret>\\"\\n        ```\\n\\n        <Admonition type=\\"note\\">\\n          You can generate the secret in the \[Auth Hooks](/dashboard/project/\_/auth/hooks) section of the Supabase dashboard.\\n        </Admonition>\\n\\n        Set the secrets in your Supabase project:\\n\\n        ```bash\\n        supabase secrets set --env-file .env\\n        ```\\n\\n        Create a new edge function:\\n\\n        ```bash\\n        supabase functions new before-user-created-hook\\n        ```\\n\\n        Add the following code to your edge function:\\n\\n        ```ts\\n        import { Webhook } from 'https://esm.sh/standardwebhooks@1.0.0'\\n\\n        const blockedProviders = \['discord']\\n\\n        Deno.serve(async (req) => {\\n          const payload = await req.text()\\n          const secret = Deno.env.get('BEFORE\_USER\_CREATED\_HOOK\_SECRET')?.replace('v1,whsec\_', '')\\n          const headers = Object.fromEntries(req.headers)\\n          const wh = new Webhook(secret)\\n\\n          try {\\n            const { user } = wh.verify(payload, headers)\\n            const provider = user.app\_metadata?.provider\\n\\n            if (blockedProviders.includes(provider)) {\\n              return new Response(\\n                JSON.stringify({\\n                  error: {\\n                    message: `Signups with ${provider} are not allowed.`,\\n                    http\_code: 403,\\n                  },\\n                }),\\n                { status: 403, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }\\n              )\\n            }\\n\\n            return new Response('{}', { status: 200, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } })\\n          } catch {\\n            return new Response('{}', { status: 400 })\\n          }\\n        })\\n        ```\\n      </TabPanel>\\n\\n      <TabPanel id=\\"http-allow-deny-by-cidr\\" label=\\"Allow/Deny by IP or CIDR\\">\\n        This example shows how you might restrict sign up from a single IP address or a range of them using \[Postgres’s built-in](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype-net-types.html) `inet` and `<<` operators for \[CIDR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classless\_Inter-Domain\_Routing) -- a method of representing IP address ranges.\\n        For instance: `123.123.123.123/32` represents only a single IP address, while `123.123.123.0/24` means all IP addresses starting with `123.123.123.`.\\n\\n        The `before-user-created` hook solves this by:\\n\\n        \*   Detecting that a user is about to be created\\n        \*   Providing the IP address in the `metadata.ip\_address` field\\n\\n        Before creating the edge function run the following snippet in your project's \[SQL Editor](/dashboard/project/\_/sql/new). This will create a `signup\_networks` table with some sample data and a `hook\_restrict\_signup\_by\_network` function to be called by the `before-user-created` auth hook.\\n\\n        ```sql SQL\_EDITOR\\n        -- Create ENUM type for network rule classification\\n        create type signup\_network\_type as enum ('allow', 'deny');\\n\\n        -- Create the signup\_networks table for controlling sign-up access by CIDR\\n        create table if not exists public.signup\_networks (\\n          id serial primary key,\\n          cidr cidr not null,\\n          type public.signup\_network\_type not null,\\n          reason text default null,\\n          note text default null,\\n          created\_at timestamp with time zone not null default now(),\\n          constraint signup\_networks\_cidr\_key unique (cidr)\\n        );\\n\\n        -- Assign appropriate permissions\\n        grant all\\n          on table public.signup\_networks\\n          to supabase\_auth\_admin;\\n\\n        revoke all\\n          on table public.signup\_networks\\n          from authenticated, anon, public;\\n\\n        -- Insert some sample data into the table\\n        insert into public.signup\_networks (cidr, type, reason, note)\\n        values\\n          ('192.0.2.0/24', 'allow', '', 'Corporate VPN'),\\n          ('198.51.100.158/32', 'deny',\\n            'Your IP Address has been blocked for abuse.',\\n            'blocked by abuse: (Ticket: ABUSE-185)'),\\n          ('203.0.113.0/24', 'deny',\\n            'Your network has been blocked for abuse.',\\n            'blocked by abuse: (Ticket: ABUSE-212)');\\n\\n        -- Create the hook function to be called by the auth server\\n        create or replace function public.hook\_restrict\_signup\_by\_network(event jsonb)\\n        returns jsonb\\n        language plpgsql\\n        as $$\\n        declare\\n          ip inet;\\n          allow\_count int;\\n          deny\_count int;\\n        begin\\n          ip := event->'metadata'->>'ip\_address';\\n\\n          -- Step 1: Check for explicit allow\\n          select count(\*) into allow\_count\\n          from public.signup\_networks\\n          where type = 'allow' and ip::inet << cidr;\\n\\n          if allow\_count > 0 then\\n            -- If explicitly allowed, allow signup\\n            return '{}'::jsonb;\\n          end if;\\n\\n          -- Step 2: Check for explicit deny\\n          select count(\*) into deny\_count\\n          from public.signup\_networks\\n          where type = 'deny' and ip::inet << cidr;\\n\\n          if deny\_count > 0 then\\n            return jsonb\_build\_object(\\n              'error', jsonb\_build\_object(\\n                'message', 'Signups are not allowed from your network.',\\n                'http\_code', 403\\n              )\\n            );\\n          end if;\\n\\n          -- Step 3: No match: allow by default\\n          return '{}'::jsonb;\\n        end;\\n        $$;\\n\\n        -- Assign permissions\\n        grant execute\\n          on function public.hook\_restrict\_signup\_by\_network\\n          to supabase\_auth\_admin;\\n\\n        revoke execute\\n          on function public.hook\_restrict\_signup\_by\_network\\n          from authenticated, anon, public;\\n        ```\\n\\n        Create a `.env` file with the following environment variables:\\n\\n        ```ini\\n        BEFORE\_USER\_CREATED\_HOOK\_SECRET=\\"v1,whsec\_<base64\_secret>\\"\\n        ```\\n\\n        <Admonition type=\\"note\\">\\n          You can generate the secret in the \[Auth Hooks](/dashboard/project/\_/auth/hooks) section of the Supabase dashboard.\\n        </Admonition>\\n\\n        Set the secrets in your Supabase project:\\n\\n        ```bash\\n        supabase secrets set --env-file .env\\n        ```\\n\\n        Create a new edge function:\\n\\n        ```bash\\n        supabase functions new before-user-created-hook\\n        ```\\n\\n        Add the following code to your edge function:\\n\\n        ```ts\\n        import { Webhook } from 'https://esm.sh/standardwebhooks@1.0.0'\\n        import { createClient } from 'https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js'\\n\\n        const whSecret = Deno.env.get('BEFORE\_USER\_CREATED\_HOOK\_SECRET')?.replace('v1,whsec\_', '')\\n        const supabaseUrl = Deno.env.get('SUPABASE\_URL')\\n        const supabaseKey = Deno.env.get('SUPABASE\_SECRET\_KEY')\\n\\n        const wh = new Webhook(whSecret)\\n        const supabase = createClient(supabaseUrl, supabaseKey)\\n\\n        Deno.serve(async (req) => {\\n          const payload = await req.text()\\n          const headers = Object.fromEntries(req.headers)\\n          try {\\n            const event = wh.verify(payload, headers)\\n\\n            // Call the same Postgres function as in the SQL example.\\n            const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc('hook\_restrict\_signup\_by\_network', {\\n              event: JSON.parse(payload),\\n            })\\n            if (error) {\\n              console.error('RPC call failed:', error)\\n              return new Response(\\n                JSON.stringify({\\n                  error: {\\n                    message: 'Internal error processing signup restriction',\\n                    http\_code: 500,\\n                  },\\n                }),\\n                {\\n                  status: 500,\\n                  headers: {\\n                    'Content-Type': 'application/json',\\n                  },\\n                }\\n              )\\n            }\\n            return new Response(JSON.stringify(data ?? {}), {\\n              status: 200,\\n              headers: {\\n                'Content-Type': 'application/json',\\n              },\\n            })\\n          } catch (err) {\\n            console.error('Webhook verification failed:', err)\\n            return new Response(\\n              JSON.stringify({\\n                error: {\\n                  message: 'Invalid request format or signature',\\n                },\\n              }),\\n              {\\n                status: 400,\\n                headers: {\\n                  'Content-Type': 'application/json',\\n                },\\n              }\\n            )\\n          }\\n        })\\n        ```\\n      </TabPanel>\\n    </Tabs>\\n  </TabPanel>\\n</Tabs>\\n"},{"title":"Configuration","href":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/branching/configuration","content":"# Configuration\\n\\nConfigure your Supabase branches using configuration as code\\n\\nThis guide covers how to configure your Supabase branches, using the `config.toml` file. In one single file, you can configure all your branches, including branch settings and secrets.\\n\\n\\n## Branch configuration with remotes\\n\\nWhen Branching is enabled, your `config.toml` settings automatically sync to all ephemeral branches through a one-to-one mapping between your Git and Supabase branches.\\n\\n\\n### Basic configuration\\n\\nTo update configuration for a Supabase branch, modify `config.toml` and push to git. The Supabase integration will detect the changes and apply them to the corresponding branch.\\n\\n\\n### Remote-specific configuration\\n\\nFor persistent branches that need specific settings, you can use the `\[remotes]` block in your `config.toml`. Each remote configuration must reference an existing project ID.\\n\\nHere's an example of configuring a separate seed script for a staging environment:\\n\\n```toml\\n\[remotes.staging]\\nproject\_id = \\"your-project-ref\\"\\n\\n\[remotes.staging.db.seed]\\nenabled = true\\nsql\_paths = \[\\"./seeds/staging.sql\\"]\\n```\\n\\nSince the `project\_id` field must reference an existing branch, you need to create the persistent branch before adding its configuration. Use the CLI to create a persistent branch first:\\n\\n```bash\\nsupabase --experimental branches create --persistent\\n# Do you want to create a branch named develop? \[Y/n]\\n```\\n\\n<Admonition type=\\"tip\\">\\n  To retrieve the project ID for an existing branch, use the `branches list` command:\\n\\n  ```bash\\n  supabase --experimental branches list\\n  ```\\n\\n  This will display a table showing all your branches with their corresponding project ID.\\n  Use the value from the `BRANCH PROJECT ID` column as your `project\_id` in the remote configuration.\\n</Admonition>\\n\\n\\n### Configuration merging\\n\\nWhen merging a PR into a persistent branch, the Supabase integration:\\n\\n1.  Checks for configuration changes\\n2.  Logs the changes\\n3.  Applies them to the target remote\\n\\nIf no remote is declared or the project ID is incorrect, the configuration step is skipped.\\n\\n\\n### Available configuration options\\n\\nAll standard configuration options are available in the `\[remotes]` block. This includes:\\n\\n\*   Database settings\\n\*   API configurations\\n\*   Authentication settings\\n\*   Edge Functions configuration\\n\*   And more\\n\\nYou can use this to maintain different configurations for different environments while keeping them all in version control.\\n\\n\\n## Managing secrets for branches\\n\\nFor sensitive configuration like SMTP credentials or API keys, you can use the Supabase CLI to manage secrets for your branches. This is especially useful for custom SMTP setup or other services that require secure credentials.\\n\\nTo set secrets for a persistent branch:\\n\\n```bash\\n# Set secrets from a .env file\\nsupabase secrets set --env-file ./supabase/.env\\n\\n# Or set individual secrets\\nsupabase secrets set SMTP\_HOST=smtp.example.com\\nsupabase secrets set SMTP\_USER=your-username\\nsupabase secrets set SMTP\_PASSWORD=your-password\\n```\\n\\nThese secrets will be available to your branch's services and can be used in your configuration. For example, in your `config.toml`:\\n\\n```toml\\n\[auth.smtp]\\nhost = \\"env(SMTP\_HOST)\\"\\nuser = \\"env(SMTP\_USER)\\"\\npassword = \\"env(SMTP\_PASSWORD)\\"\\n```\\n\\n<Admonition type=\\"note\\" title=\\"Secrets are branch-specific\\">\\n  Secrets set for one branch are not automatically available in other branches. You'll need to set them separately for each branch that needs them.\\n</Admonition>\\n\\n\\n### Using dotenvx for git-based workflow\\n\\nFor managing environment variables across different branches, you can use \[dotenvx](https://dotenvx.com/) to securely manage your configurations. This approach is particularly useful for teams working with Git branches and preview deployments.\\n\\n\\n#### Environment file structure\\n\\nFollowing the conventions used in the \[example repository](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/master/examples/slack-clone/nextjs-slack-clone-dotenvx/README.md), environments are configured using dotenv files in the `supabase` directory:\\n\\n| File            | Environment | `.gitignore` it? | Encrypted |\\n| --------------- | ----------- | ---------------- | --------- |\\n| .env.keys       | All         | Yes              | No        |\\n| .env.local      | Local       | Yes              | No        |\\n| .env.production | Production  | No               | Yes       |\\n| .env.preview    | Branches    | No               | Yes       |\\n| .env            | Any         | Maybe            | Yes       |\\n\\n\\n#### Setting up encrypted secrets\\n\\n1.  Generate key pair and encrypt your secrets:\\n\\n```bash\\nnpx @dotenvx/dotenvx set SUPABASE\_AUTH\_EXTERNAL\_GITHUB\_SECRET \\"<your-secret>\\" -f supabase/.env.preview\\n```\\n\\nThis creates a new encryption key in `supabase/.env.preview` and a new decryption key in `supabase/.env.keys`.\\n\\n2.  Update project secrets:\\n\\n```bash\\nnpx supabase secrets set --env-file supabase/.env.keys\\n```\\n\\n3.  Choose your configuration approach in `config.toml`:\\n\\nOption A: Use encrypted values directly:\\n\\n```toml\\n\[auth.external.github]\\nenabled = true\\nsecret = \\"encrypted:<encrypted-value>\\"\\n```\\n\\nOption B: Use environment variables:\\n\\n```toml\\n\[auth.external.github]\\nenabled = true\\nclient\_id = \\"env(SUPABASE\_AUTH\_EXTERNAL\_GITHUB\_CLIENT\_ID)\\"\\nsecret = \\"env(SUPABASE\_AUTH\_EXTERNAL\_GITHUB\_SECRET)\\"\\n```\\n\\n<Admonition type=\\"note\\" title=\\"Secret fields\\">\\n  The `encrypted:` syntax only works for designated \\"secret\\" fields in the configuration. Using encrypted values in other fields will not be automatically decrypted and may cause issues. For non-secret fields, use environment variables with the `env()` syntax instead.\\n\\n  The following fields support the `encrypted:` syntax:\\n\\n  \*\*Studio\*\*\\n\\n  \*   `studio.openai\_api\_key`\\n\\n  \*\*Database\*\*\\n\\n  \*   `db.root\_key`\\n  \*   `db.vault.\*` (any key in the vault map)\\n\\n  \*\*Auth - Core Keys\*\*\\n\\n  \*   `auth.publishable\_key`\\n  \*   `auth.secret\_key`\\n  \*   `auth.jwt\_secret`\\n\\n  \*\*Auth - Email (SMTP)\*\*\\n\\n  \*   `auth.email.smtp.pass`\\n\\n  \*\*Auth - Captcha\*\*\\n\\n  \*   `auth.captcha.secret`\\n\\n  \*\*Auth - Hooks\*\*\\n\\n  \*   `auth.hook.mfa\_verification\_attempt.secrets`\\n  \*   `auth.hook.password\_verification\_attempt.secrets`\\n  \*   `auth.hook.custom\_access\_token.secrets`\\n  \*   `auth.hook.send\_sms.secrets`\\n  \*   `auth.hook.send\_email.secrets`\\n  \*   `auth.hook.before\_user\_created.secrets`\\n\\n  \*\*Auth - SMS Providers\*\*\\n\\n  \*   `auth.sms.twilio.auth\_token`\\n  \*   `auth.sms.twilio\_verify.auth\_token`\\n  \*   `auth.sms.messagebird.access\_key`\\n  \*   `auth.sms.textlocal.api\_key`\\n  \*   `auth.sms.vonage.api\_secret`\\n\\n  \*\*Auth - External OAuth Providers\*\*\\n\\n  \*   `auth.external.\*.secret`\\n\\n  \*\*Edge Runtime\*\*\\n\\n  \*   `edge\_runtime.secrets.\*` (any key in the secrets map)\\n</Admonition>\\n\\n\\n#### Using with preview branches\\n\\nWhen you commit your `.env.preview` file with encrypted values, the branching executor will automatically retrieve and use these values when deploying your branch. This allows you to maintain different configurations for different branches while keeping sensitive information secure.\\n\\n\\n## Configuration examples\\n\\n\\n### Multi-environment setup\\n\\nHere's an example of a complete multi-environment configuration:\\n\\n```toml\\n# Default configuration for all branches\\n\[api]\\nenabled = true\\nport = 54321\\nschemas = \[\\"public\\", \\"storage\\", \\"graphql\_public\\"]\\n\\n\[db]\\nport = 54322\\npool\_size = 10\\n\\n# Staging-specific configuration\\n\[remotes.staging]\\nproject\_id = \\"staging-project-ref\\"\\n\\n\[remotes.staging.api]\\nmax\_rows = 1000\\n\\n\[remotes.staging.db.seed]\\nsql\_paths = \[\\"./seeds/staging.sql\\"]\\n\\n# Production-specific configuration\\n\[remotes.production]\\nproject\_id = \\"prod-project-ref\\"\\n\\n\[remotes.production.api]\\nmax\_rows = 500\\n\\n\[remotes.production.db]\\npool\_size = 25\\n```\\n\\n<Admonition type=\\"tip\\">\\n  To retrieve the project ID for an existing branch, use the `branches list` command:\\n\\n  ```bash\\n  supabase --experimental branches list\\n  ```\\n\\n  This will display a table showing all your branches with their corresponding project ID.\\n  Use the value from the `BRANCH PROJECT ID` column as your `project\_id` in the remote configuration.\\n</Admonition>\\n\\n\\n### Feature branch configuration\\n\\nFor feature branches that need specific settings:\\n\\n```toml\\n\[remotes.feature-oauth]\\nproject\_id = \\"feature-branch-ref\\"\\n\\n\[remotes.feature-oauth.auth.external.google]\\nenabled = true\\nclient\_id = \\"env(GOOGLE\_CLIENT\_ID)\\"\\nsecret = \\"env(GOOGLE\_CLIENT\_SECRET)\\"\\n```\\n\\n<Admonition type=\\"tip\\">\\n  To retrieve the project ID for an existing branch, use the `branches list` command:\\n\\n  ```bash\\n  supabase --experimental branches list\\n  ```\\n\\n  This will display a table showing all your branches with their corresponding project ID.\\n  Use the value from the `BRANCH PROJECT ID` column as your `project\_id` in the remote configuration.\\n</Admonition>\\n\\n\\n## Next steps\\n\\n\*   Explore \[branching integrations](/docs/guides/deployment/branching/integrations)\\n\*   Learn about \[troubleshooting branches](/docs/guides/deployment/branching/troubleshooting)\\n\*   Review \[branching pricing](/docs/guides/platform/manage-your-usage/branching#pricing)\\n"}]},"storage":{"nodes":\[{"title":"Storage Buckets","href":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/buckets/fundamentals","content":"# Storage Buckets\\n\\n\\n\\nBuckets allow you to keep your files organized and determines the \[Access Model](#access-model) for your assets. \[Upload restrictions](/docs/guides/storage/buckets/creating-buckets#restricting-uploads) like max file size and allowed content types are also defined at the bucket level.\\n\\n\\n## Access model\\n\\nThere are 2 access models for buckets, \*\*public\*\* and \*\*private\*\* buckets.\\n\\n\\n### Private buckets\\n\\nWhen a bucket is set to \*\*Private\*\* all operations are subject to access control via \[RLS policies](/docs/guides/storage/security/access-control). This also applies when downloading assets. Buckets are private by default.\\n\\nThe only ways to download assets within a private bucket is to:\\n\\n\*   Use the \[download method](/docs/reference/javascript/storage-from-download) by providing an authorization header containing your user's JWT. The RLS policy you create on the `storage.objects` table will use this user to determine if they have access.\\n\*   Create a signed URL with the \[`createSignedUrl` method](/docs/reference/javascript/storage-from-createsignedurl) that can be accessed for a limited time.\\n\\n\\n#### Example use cases:\\n\\n\*   Uploading users' sensitive documents\\n\*   Securing private assets by using RLS to set up fine-grain access controls\\n\\n\\n### Public buckets\\n\\nWhen a bucket is designated as 'Public,' it effectively bypasses access controls for both retrieving and serving files within the bucket. This means that anyone who possesses the asset URL can readily access the file.\\n\\nAccess control is still enforced for other types of operations including uploading, deleting, moving, and copying.\\n\\n\\n#### Example use cases:\\n\\n\*   User profile pictures\\n\*   User public media\\n\*   Blog post content\\n\\nPublic buckets are more performant than private buckets since they are \[cached differently](/docs/guides/storage/cdn/fundamentals#public-vs-private-buckets).\\n"},{"title":"Storage Access Control","href":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/security/access-control","content":"# Storage Access Control\\n\\n\\n\\nSupabase Storage is designed to work perfectly with Postgres \[Row Level Security](/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security) (RLS).\\n\\nYou can use RLS to create \[Security Access Policies](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createpolicy.html) that are incredibly powerful and flexible, allowing you to restrict access based on your business needs.\\n\\n\\n## Access policies\\n\\nBy default Storage does not allow any uploads to buckets without RLS policies. You selectively allow certain operations by creating RLS policies on the `storage.objects` table.\\n\\nYou can find the documentation for the storage schema \[here](/docs/guides/storage/schema/design) , and to simplify the process of crafting your policies, you can utilize these \[helper functions](/docs/guides/storage/schema/helper-functions) .\\n\\nIf you need different `SELECT` policies for different Storage actions, such as listing objects versus reading authenticated objects, use the operation-aware helpers `storage.allow\_only\_operation()` and `storage.allow\_any\_operation()` documented in \[Storage Helper Functions](/docs/guides/storage/schema/helper-functions).\\n\\n<Admonition type=\\"note\\">\\n  The RLS policies required for different operations are documented \[here](/docs/reference/javascript/storage-createbucket)\\n</Admonition>\\n\\nFor example, the only RLS policy required for \[uploading](/docs/reference/javascript/storage-from-upload) objects is to grant the `INSERT` permission to the `storage.objects` table.\\n\\nTo allow overwriting files using the `upsert` functionality you will need to additionally grant `SELECT` and `UPDATE` permissions.\\n\\n\\n## Policy examples\\n\\nAn easy way to get started would be to create RLS policies for `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE` operations and restrict the policies to meet your security requirements. For example, one can start with the following `INSERT` policy:\\n\\n```sql\\ncreate policy \\"policy\_name\\"\\nON storage.objects\\nfor insert with check (\\n  true\\n);\\n```\\n\\nand modify it to only allow authenticated users to upload assets to a specific bucket by changing it to:\\n\\n```sql\\ncreate policy \\"policy\_name\\"\\non storage.objects for insert to authenticated with check (\\n    -- restrict bucket\\n    bucket\_id = 'my\_bucket\_id'\\n);\\n```\\n\\nThis example demonstrates how you would allow authenticated users to upload files to a folder called `private` inside `my\_bucket\_id`:\\n\\n```sql\\ncreate policy \\"Allow authenticated uploads\\"\\non storage.objects\\nfor insert\\nto authenticated\\nwith check (\\n  bucket\_id = 'my\_bucket\_id' and\\n  (storage.foldername(name))\[1] = 'private'\\n);\\n```\\n\\nThis example demonstrates how you would allow authenticated users to upload files to a folder called with their `users.id` inside `my\_bucket\_id`:\\n\\n```sql\\ncreate policy \\"Allow authenticated uploads\\"\\non storage.objects\\nfor insert\\nto authenticated\\nwith check (\\n  bucket\_id = 'my\_bucket\_id' and\\n  (storage.foldername(name))\[1] = (select auth.jwt()->>'sub')\\n);\\n```\\n\\nAllow a user to access a file that was previously uploaded by the same user:\\n\\n```sql\\ncreate policy \\"Individual user Access\\"\\non storage.objects for select\\nto authenticated\\nusing ( (select auth.jwt()->>'sub') = owner\_id );\\n```\\n\\nAllow anyone to access objects in the `avatars` bucket via publishable key. The `allow\_any\_operation()` filter is critical here as without it users would be able to list the bucket contents.\\n\\n<Admonition type=\\"note\\">\\n  This is not needed for public buckets, as they are already publicly accessible\\n</Admonition>\\n\\n```sql\\ncreate policy \\"Avatar images are publicly accessible.\\" on storage.objects\\n  for select using (bucket\_id = 'avatars' and storage.allow\_any\_operation(array\['object.get\_authenticated\_info', 'object.get\_authenticated']));\\n```\\n\\n\*\*\*\\n\\n{/\* Finish with a video. This also appears in the Sidebar via the \\"tocVideo\\" metadata \*/}\\n\\n<div className=\\"video-container\\">\\n  <iframe src=\\"https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/4ERX\_\_Y908k\\" frameBorder=\\"1\\" allow=\\"accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture\\" allowFullScreen />\\n</div>\\n\\n\\n## Bypassing access controls\\n\\nIf you exclusively use Storage from trusted clients, such as your own servers, and need to bypass the RLS policies, you can use the `service key` in the `Authorization` header. Service keys entirely bypass RLS policies, granting you unrestricted access to all Storage APIs.\\n\\nRemember you should not share the service key publicly.\\n"},{"title":"Build a User Management App with Angular","href":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/tutorials/with-angular","content":"# Build a User Management App with Angular\\n\\n\\n\\nThis tutorial demonstrates how to build a basic user management app. The app authenticates and identifies the user, stores their profile information in the database, and allows the user to log in, update their profile details, and upload a profile photo. The app uses:\\n\\n\*   \[Supabase Database](/docs/guides/database) - a Postgres database for storing your user data and \[Row Level Security](/docs/guides/auth#row-level-security) so data is protected and users can only access their own information.\\n\*   \[Supabase Auth](/docs/guides/auth) - allow users to sign up and log in.\\n\*   \[Supabase Storage](/docs/guides/storage) - allow users to upload a profile photo.\\n\\n!\[Supabase User Management example](/docs/img/user-management-demo.png)\\n\\n<Admonition type=\\"note\\">\\n  If you get stuck while working through this guide, you can find the \[full example on GitHub](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/tree/master/examples/user-management/angular-user-management).\\n</Admonition>\\n\\n\\n## Project setup\\n\\nBefore you start building you need to set up the Database and API. You can do this by starting a new Project in Supabase and then creating a \\"schema\\" inside the database.\\n\\n\\n### Create a project\\n\\n1.  \[Create a new project](/dashboard) in the Supabase Dashboard.\\n2.  Enter your project details.\\n3.  Wait for the new database to launch.\\n\\n\\n### Set up the database schema\\n\\nNow set up the database schema. You can use the \\"User Management Starter\\" quickstart in the SQL Editor, or you can copy/paste the SQL from below and run it.\\n\\n<Tabs scrollable size=\\"small\\" type=\\"underlined\\" defaultActiveId=\\"dashboard\\" queryGroup=\\"database-method\\">\\n  <TabPanel id=\\"dashboard\\" label=\\"Dashboard\\">\\n    1.  Go to the \[SQL Editor](/dashboard/project/\_/sql) page in the Dashboard.\\n    2.  Click \*\*User Management Starter\*\* under the \*\*Community > Quickstarts\*\* tab.\\n    3.  Click \*\*Run\*\*.\\n\\n    <Admonition type=\\"note\\">\\n      You can pull the database schema down to your local project by running the `db pull` command. Read the \[local development docs](/docs/guides/cli/local-development#link-your-project) for detailed instructions.\\n\\n      ```bash\\n      supabase link --project-ref <project-id>\\n      # You can get <project-id> from your project's dashboard URL: https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/<project-id>\\n      supabase db pull\\n      ```\\n    </Admonition>\\n  </TabPanel>\\n\\n  <TabPanel id=\\"sql\\" label=\\"SQL\\">\\n    <Admonition type=\\"note\\">\\n      When working locally you can run the following command to create a new migration file:\\n    </Admonition>\\n\\n    ```bash\\n    supabase migration new user\_management\_starter\\n    ```\\n\\n    ```sql\\n    -- Create a table for public profiles\\n    create table profiles (\\n      id uuid references auth.users not null primary key,\\n      updated\_at timestamp with time zone,\\n      username text unique,\\n      full\_name text,\\n      avatar\_url text,\\n      website text,\\n\\n      constraint username\_length check (char\_length(username) >= 3)\\n    );\\n\\n    -- Grant the privileges roles need\\n    GRANT SELECT ON public.profiles TO anon;\\n    GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON public.profiles TO authenticated;\\n\\n    -- Set up Row Level Security (RLS)\\n    -- See https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security for more details.\\n    alter table profiles\\n      enable row level security;\\n\\n    create policy \\"Public profiles are viewable by everyone.\\" on profiles\\n      for select using (true);\\n\\n    create policy \\"Users can insert their own profile.\\" on profiles\\n      for insert with check ((select auth.uid()) = id);\\n\\n    create policy \\"Users can update own profile.\\" on profiles\\n      for update using ((select auth.uid()) = id);\\n\\n    -- This trigger automatically creates a profile entry when a new user signs up via Supabase Auth.\\n    -- See https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/managing-user-data#using-triggers for more details.\\n    create function public.handle\_new\_user()\\n    returns trigger\\n    set search\_path = ''\\n    as $$\\n    begin\\n      insert into public.profiles (id, full\_name, avatar\_url)\\n      values (new.id, new.raw\_user\_meta\_data->>'full\_name', new.raw\_user\_meta\_data->>'avatar\_url');\\n      return new;\\n    end;\\n    $$ language plpgsql security definer;\\n    create trigger on\_auth\_user\_created\\n      after insert on auth.users\\n      for each row execute procedure public.handle\_new\_user();\\n\\n    -- Set up Storage!\\n    insert into storage.buckets (id, name)\\n      values ('avatars', 'avatars');\\n\\n    -- Set up access controls for storage. Allows downloading object with public key\\n    -- See https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/security/access-control#policy-examples for more details.\\n    create policy \\"Avatar images are publicly accessible.\\" on storage.objects\\n      for select using (bucket\_id = 'avatars' and storage.allow\_any\_operation(array\['object.get\_authenticated\_info', 'object.get\_authenticated']));\\n\\n    create policy \\"Anyone can upload an avatar.\\" on storage.objects\\n      for insert with check (bucket\_id = 'avatars');\\n\\n    create policy \\"Anyone can update their own avatar.\\" on storage.objects\\n      for update using ((select auth.uid()) = owner) with check (bucket\_id = 'avatars');\\n    ```\\n  </TabPanel>\\n</Tabs>\\n\\n\\n### Get API details\\n\\nNow that you've created some database tables, you are ready to insert data using the auto-generated API.\\n\\nTo do this, you need to get the Project URL and key from \[the project \*\*Connect\*\* dialog](/dashboard/project/\_?showConnect=true\\\\\&connectTab=mobiles\\\\\&framework=ionicangular).\\n\\n\[Read the API keys docs](/docs/guides/getting-started/api-keys) for a full explanation of all key types and their uses.\\n\\n<Admonition type=\\"note\\" title=\\"Changes to API keys\\">\\n  Supabase is changing the way keys work to improve project security and developer experience. You can \[read the full announcement on GitHub](https://github.com/orgs/supabase/discussions/29260).\\n\\n  The older `anon` and `service\_role` keys will work until the end of 2026 but \*\*we strongly encourage switching to and using\*\* the new publishable (`sb\_publishable\_xxx`) and secret (`sb\_secret\_xxx`) keys now.\\n\\n  In most cases, you can get keys from \[the Project's \*\*Connect\*\* dialog](/dashboard/project/\_?showConnect=true\\\\\&connectTab=mobiles\\\\\&framework=ionicangular), but if you want a specific key, you can find them in the \[\*\*Settings > API Keys\*\*](/dashboard/project/\_/settings/api-keys/) section of the Dashboard.\\n\\n  \*   \*\*For legacy keys\*\*, copy the `anon` key for client-side operations and the `service\_role` key for server-side operations from the \*\*Legacy API Keys\*\* tab.\\n  \*   \*\*For new keys\*\*, open the \*\*API Keys\*\* tab, if you don't have a publishable key already, click \*\*Create new API Keys\*\*, and copy the value from the \*\*Publishable key\*\* section.\\n</Admonition>\\n\\n\\n## Building the app\\n\\nStart with building the Angular app from scratch.\\n\\n\\n### Initialize an Angular app\\n\\nUse the \[Angular CLI](https://angular.io/cli) to initialize an app called `supabase-angular` setting some defaults that you can change to suit your needs:\\n\\n```bash\\nnpx ng new supabase-angular --routing false --style css --standalone false --ssr false\\ncd supabase-angular\\n```\\n\\nInstall \[supabase-js](https://github.com/supabase/supabase-js):\\n\\n```bash\\nnpm install @supabase/supabase-js\\n```\\n\\nCreate a `src/environments` directory and save API URL and key that you copied \[earlier](#get-api-details) as environment variables in a new `src/environments/environment.ts` file.\\n\\nThe application exposes these variables in the browser, and that's fine as Supabase enables \[Row Level Security](/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security) by default on all tables.\\n\\n<CodeSampleWrapper source=\\"https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/master/examples/user-management/angular-user-management/src/environments/environment.ts\\">\\n  <NamedCodeBlock name=\\"src/environments/environment.ts\\">\\n    ```typescript name=src/environments/environment.ts\\n    export const environment = {\\n      production: false,\\n      supabaseUrl: 'YOUR\_SUPABASE\_URL',\\n      supabasePublishableKey: 'YOUR\_SUPABASE\_PUBLISHABLE\_KEY',\\n    }\\n    ```\\n  </NamedCodeBlock>\\n</CodeSampleWrapper>\\n\\nWith the API credentials in place, create a `SupabaseService` with `ng g s supabase` and add the following code to initialize the Supabase client and implement functions to communicate with the Supabase API.\\n\\n<CodeSampleWrapper source=\\"https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/master/examples/user-management/angular-user-management/src/app/supabase.service.ts\\">\\n  <NamedCodeBlock name=\\"src/app/supabase.service.ts\\">\\n    ```typescript name=src/app/supabase.service.ts\\n    import { Injectable } from '@angular/core'\\n    import { AuthChangeEvent, createClient, Session, SupabaseClient, User } from '@supabase/supabase-js'\\n    import { environment } from '../environments/environment'\\n\\n    export interface Profile {\\n      id?: string\\n      username: string\\n      website: string\\n      avatar\_url: string\\n    }\\n\\n    @Injectable({\\n      providedIn: 'root',\\n    })\\n    export class SupabaseService {\\n      private supabase: SupabaseClient\\n\\n      constructor() {\\n        this.supabase = createClient(environment.supabaseUrl, environment.supabasePublishableKey)\\n      }\\n\\n      async getUser(): Promise<User | null> {\\n        const { data, error } = await this.supabase.auth.getUser()\\n        if (error) {\\n          return null\\n        }\\n        return data.user\\n      }\\n\\n      profile(user: User) {\\n        return this.supabase\\n          .from('profiles')\\n          .select(`username, website, avatar\_url`)\\n          .eq('id', user.id)\\n          .single()\\n      }\\n\\n      authChanges(callback: (event: AuthChangeEvent, session: Session | null) => void) {\\n        return this.supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange(callback)\\n      }\\n\\n      signIn(email: string) {\\n        return this.supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email })\\n      }\\n\\n      signOut() {\\n        return this.supabase.auth.signOut()\\n      }\\n\\n      updateProfile(profile: Profile) {\\n        const update = {\\n          ...profile,\\n          updated\_at: new Date(),\\n        }\\n\\n        return this.supabase.from('profiles').upsert(update)\\n      }\\n\\n      downLoadImage(path: string) {\\n        return this.supabase.storage.from('avatars').download(path)\\n      }\\n\\n      uploadAvatar(filePath: string, file: File) {\\n        return this.supabase.storage.from('avatars').upload(filePath, file)\\n      }\\n    }\\n    ```\\n  </NamedCodeBlock>\\n</CodeSampleWrapper>\\n\\nOptionally, update `src/styles.css` to style the app. You can find the full contents of this file \[in the example repository](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/tree/master/examples/user-management/angular-user-management/src/styles.css).\\n\\n\\n### Set up a login component\\n\\nYou need an Angular component to manage logins and sign ups. The component uses \[Magic Links](/docs/guides/auth/auth-email-passwordless#with-magic-link), so users can sign in with their email without using passwords.\\n\\n<Admonition type=\\"tip\\" title=\\"Did you know?\\">\\n  You can customize other emails sent out to new users, including the email's looks, content, and query parameters from \[the \*\*Authentication > Email\*\*](/dashboard/project/\_/auth/templates) section of the Dashboard.\\n</Admonition>\\n\\nCreate an `AuthComponent` with the `ng g c auth` Angular CLI command and add the following code.\\n\\n<Tabs listClassNames=\\"flex-nowrap overflow-x-auto -mb-6\\">\\n  <TabPanel id=\\"src/app/auth/auth.component.ts\\" label=\\"src/app/auth/auth.component.ts\\">\\n    <CodeSampleWrapper source=\\"https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/master/examples/user-management/angular-user-management/src/app/auth/auth.component.ts\\">\\n      ```typescript name=src/app/auth/auth.component.ts\\n      import { Component } from '@angular/core'\\n      import { FormBuilder, FormGroup } from '@angular/forms'\\n      import { SupabaseService } from '../supabase.service'\\n\\n      @Component({\\n        selector: 'app-auth',\\n        templateUrl: './auth.component.html',\\n        styleUrls: \['./auth.component.css'],\\n        standalone: false,\\n      })\\n      export class AuthComponent {\\n        loading = false\\n        signInForm: FormGroup\\n\\n        constructor(\\n          private readonly supabase: SupabaseService,\\n          private readonly formBuilder: FormBuilder\\n        ) {\\n          this.signInForm = this.formBuilder.group({\\n            email: '',\\n          })\\n        }\\n\\n        async onSubmit(): Promise<void> {\\n          try {\\n            this.loading = true\\n            const email = this.signInForm.value.email as string\\n            const { error } = await this.supabase.signIn(email)\\n            if (error) throw error\\n            alert('Check your email for the login link!')\\n          } catch (error) {\\n            if (error instanceof Error) {\\n              alert(error.message)\\n            }\\n          } finally {\\n            this.signInForm.reset()\\n            this.loading = false\\n          }\\n        }\\n      }\\n      ```\\n    </CodeSampleWrapper>\\n  </TabPanel>\\n\\n  <TabPanel id=\\"src/app/auth/auth.component.html\\" label=\\"src/app/auth/auth.component.html\\">\\n    <CodeSampleWrapper source=\\"https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/master/examples/user-management/angular-user-management/src/app/auth/auth.component.html\\">\\n      ```\\n      <div class=\\"row flex-center flex\\">\\n        <div class=\\"col-6 form-widget\\" aria-live=\\"polite\\">\\n          <h1 class=\\"header\\">Supabase + Angular</h1>\\n          <p class=\\"description\\">Sign in via magic link with your email below</p>\\n          <form \[formGroup]=\\"signInForm\\" (ngSubmit)=\\"onSubmit()\\" class=\\"form-widget\\">\\n            <div>\\n              <label for=\\"email\\">Email</label>\\n              <input\\n                id=\\"email\\"\\n                formControlName=\\"email\\"\\n                class=\\"inputField\\"\\n                type=\\"email\\"\\n                placeholder=\\"Your email\\"\\n              />\\n            </div>\\n            <div>\\n              <button type=\\"submit\\" class=\\"button block\\" \[disabled]=\\"loading\\">\\n                {{ loading ? \\"Loading\\" : \\"Send magic link\\" }}\\n              </button>\\n            </div>\\n          </form>\\n        </div>\\n      </div>\\n      ```\\n    </CodeSampleWrapper>\\n  </TabPanel>\\n</Tabs>\\n\\n\\n### Account page\\n\\nUsers also need a way to edit their profile details and manage their accounts after signing in. Create an `AccountComponent` with the `ng g c account` Angular CLI command and add the following code.\\n\\n<Tabs listClassNames=\\"flex-nowrap overflow-x-auto -mb-6\\">\\n  <TabPanel id=\\"src/app/account/account.component.ts\\" label=\\"src/app/account/account.component.ts\\">\\n    <CodeSampleWrapper source=\\"https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/master/examples/user-management/angular-user-management/src/app/account/account.component.ts\\">\\n      ```typescript name=src/app/account/account.component.ts\\n      import { Component, Input, OnInit } from '@angular/core'\\n      import { FormBuilder, FormGroup } from '@angular/forms'\\n      import { User } from '@supabase/supabase-js'\\n      import { Profile, SupabaseService } from '../supabase.service'\\n\\n      @Component({\\n        selector: 'app-account',\\n        templateUrl: './account.component.html',\\n        styleUrls: \['./account.component.css'],\\n        standalone: false,\\n      })\\n      export class AccountComponent implements OnInit {\\n        loading = false\\n        profile!: Profile\\n        updateProfileForm!: FormGroup\\n\\n\\n      // ...\\n\\n\\n        @Input()\\n        user!: User\\n\\n        constructor(\\n          private readonly supabase: SupabaseService,\\n          private formBuilder: FormBuilder\\n        ) {\\n          this.updateProfileForm = this.formBuilder.group({\\n            username: '',\\n            website: '',\\n            avatar\_url: '',\\n          })\\n        }\\n\\n        async ngOnInit(): Promise<void> {\\n          await this.getProfile()\\n\\n          const { username, website, avatar\_url } = this.profile\\n          this.updateProfileForm.patchValue({\\n            username,\\n            website,\\n            avatar\_url,\\n          })\\n        }\\n\\n        async getProfile() {\\n          try {\\n            this.loading = true\\n            const { data: profile, error, status } = await this.supabase.profile(this.user)\\n\\n            if (error \&\& status !== 406) {\\n              throw error\\n            }\\n\\n            if (profile) {\\n              this.profile = profile\\n            }\\n          } catch (error) {\\n            if (error instanceof Error) {\\n              alert(error.message)\\n            }\\n          } finally {\\n            this.loading = false\\n          }\\n        }\\n\\n        async updateProfile(): Promise<void> {\\n          try {\\n            this.loading = true\\n\\n            const username = this.updateProfileForm.value.username as string\\n            const website = this.updateProfileForm.value.website as string\\n            const avatar\_url = this.updateProfileForm.value.avatar\_url as string\\n\\n            const { error } = await this.supabase.updateProfile({\\n              id: this.user.id,\\n              username,\\n              website,\\n              avatar\_url,\\n            })\\n            if (error) throw error\\n          } catch (error) {\\n            if (error instanceof Error) {\\n              alert(error.message)\\n            }\\n          } finally {\\n            this.loading = false\\n          }\\n        }\\n\\n        async signOut() {\\n          await this.supabase.signOut()\\n        }\\n      }\\n      ```\\n    </CodeSampleWrapper>\\n  </TabPanel>\\n\\n  <TabPanel id=\\"src/app/account/account.component.html\\" label=\\"src/app/account/account.component.html\\">\\n    <CodeSampleWrapper source=\\"https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/master/examples/user-management/angular-user-management/src/app/account/account.component.html\\">\\n      ```\\n      <form \[formGroup]=\\"updateProfileForm\\" (ngSubmit)=\\"updateProfile()\\" class=\\"form-widget\\">\\n\\n        // ...\\n\\n        <div>\\n          <label for=\\"email\\">Email</label>\\n          <input id=\\"email\\" type=\\"text\\" \[value]=\\"user.email\\" disabled />\\n        </div>\\n        <div>\\n          <label for=\\"username\\">Name</label>\\n          <input formControlName=\\"username\\" id=\\"username\\" type=\\"text\\" />\\n        </div>\\n        <div>\\n          <label for=\\"website\\">Website</label>\\n          <input formControlName=\\"website\\" id=\\"website\\" type=\\"url\\" />\\n        </div>\\n\\n        <div>\\n          <button type=\\"submit\\" class=\\"button primary block\\" \[disabled]=\\"loading\\">\\n            {{ loading ? \\"Loading ...\\" : \\"Update\\" }}\\n          </button>\\n        </div>\\n\\n        <div>\\n          <button class=\\"button block\\" (click)=\\"signOut()\\">Sign Out</button>\\n        </div>\\n      </form>\\n      ```\\n    </CodeSampleWrapper>\\n  </TabPanel>\\n</Tabs>\\n\\n\\n## Profile photos\\n\\nAdd a way for users to upload a profile photo. Supabase configures every project with \[Storage](/docs/guides/storage) for managing large files like photos and videos.\\n\\n\\n### Create an upload widget\\n\\nCreate an `AvatarComponent` with the `ng g c avatar` Angular CLI command and add the following code.\\n\\n<Tabs listClassNames=\\"flex-nowrap overflow-x-auto -mb-6\\">\\n  <TabPanel id=\\"src/app/avatar/avatar.component.ts\\" label=\\"src/app/avatar/avatar.component.ts\\">\\n    <CodeSampleWrapper source=\\"https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/master/examples/user-management/angular-user-management/src/app/avatar/avatar.component.ts\\">\\n      ```typescript name=src/app/avatar/avatar.component.ts\\n      import { Component, EventEmitter, Input, Output } from '@angular/core'\\n      import { SafeResourceUrl, DomSanitizer } from '@angular/platform-browser'\\n      import { SupabaseService } from '../supabase.service'\\n\\n      @Component({\\n        selector: 'app-avatar',\\n        templateUrl: './avatar.component.html',\\n        styleUrls: \['./avatar.component.css'],\\n        standalone: false,\\n      })\\n      export class AvatarComponent {\\n        \_avatarUrl: SafeResourceUrl | undefined\\n        uploading = false\\n\\n        @Input()\\n        set avatarUrl(url: string | null) {\\n          if (url) {\\n            this.downloadImage(url)\\n          }\\n        }\\n\\n        @Output() upload = new EventEmitter<string>()\\n\\n        constructor(\\n          private readonly supabase: SupabaseService,\\n          private readonly dom: DomSanitizer\\n        ) {}\\n\\n        async downloadImage(path: string) {\\n          try {\\n            const { data } = await this.supabase.downLoadImage(path)\\n            if (data instanceof Blob) {\\n              this.\_avatarUrl = this.dom.bypassSecurityTrustResourceUrl(URL.createObjectURL(data))\\n            }\\n          } catch (error) {\\n            if (error instanceof Error) {\\n              console.error('Error downloading image: ', error.message)\\n            }\\n          }\\n        }\\n\\n        async uploadAvatar(event: any) {\\n          try {\\n            this.uploading = true\\n            if (!event.target.files || event.target.files.length === 0) {\\n              throw new Error('You must select an image to upload.')\\n            }\\n\\n            const file = Supabase Auth SDK contains three different functions for authenticating user access to applications:\\n\\n\\n### Summary of the methods\\n\\n\*   Use \[`getClaims`](/docs/reference/javascript/auth-getclaims) to protect pages and user data. It reads the access token from storage and verifies it. Locally via the \[WebCrypto API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web\_Crypto\_API) and a cached JWKS endpoint when the project uses asymmetric signing keys (the default for new projects), or by calling `getUser` solely to validate when symmetric keys are in use. The returned claims always come from decoding the JWT, not from a user lookup.\\n\*   \[`getUser`](/docs/reference/javascript/auth-getuser) makes a network call to the project's Auth instance to get the user record, which includes the most up-to-date information about the user at the cost of a network call.\\n\*   \[`getSession`](/docs/reference/javascript/auth-getsession) when you need the raw session (the access token, refresh token, and expiry). For example to forward the access token to another service. The session is loaded directly from local storage and isn't re-validated against the Auth server, so the embedded user object shouldn't be trusted on its own when storage is shared with the client (cookies, request headers). To verify identity, validate the access token with `getClaims`, or call `getUser` for a fresh, server-confirmed user record.\\n\\n\*\*In summary\*\*: use `getClaims` to verify identity (typically for protecting pages and data), `getUser` when you need an up-to-date user record from the Auth server, and `getSession` when you need the access or refresh token directly, but don't rely on the user object it returns for authorization decisions.\\n\\n<Tabs listClassNames=\\"flex-nowrap overflow-x-auto -mb-6\\">\\n  <TabPanel id=\\"src/app/app.component.ts\\"    this.user = await this.supabase.getUser()\\n          this.supabase.authChanges(async () => {\\n            this.user = await this.supabase.getUser()\\n          })\\n        }\\n      }\\n
